newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan watchdog declines comment on Nomura case.
newsitem.headline: Japan watchdog declines comment on Nomura case.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog declined to comment on Friday on whether it was considering seeking legal action against Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
"We have no comment," an official of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) told Reuters.
Asked if the SESC planned to make any announcements on Friday, he said: "We will not comment on issues related to Nomura."
Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, said on Thursday that two of its directors had been involved in an "apparently irregular" deal with a corporate client and that the SESC was investigating the case.
Nomura said the probe was into transactions made through the client's account several times without the client's approval.

Kyodo news service, quoting "financial sources", said on Friday that the SESC may file a complaint against Nomura with the Tokyo District Public Prosecutor's Office. In Japan, the filing of such a complaint is the first step in launching legal action.
